hub_intro_html:
Fresno is the largest city in the Central Valley and the seat of Fresno County — a metro of half a million people whose economy still runs on what the surrounding farmland produces. Ag packing and processing plants, cold storage warehouses, distribution hubs strung along Highway 99, retail corridors like Blackstone Avenue, and a downtown office core all share one thing in common: enormous amounts of flat and low-slope roof baking under some of the harshest sun in California. Allstate Spray Foam has been protecting those roofs for more than twenty years. We are a family-owned spray polyurethane foam (SPF) contractor — Fully Licensed · Lic #C-2-1052735, BBB Accredited, and a member of the Spray Polyurethane Foam Alliance — and our crews dispatch to Fresno jobs about 45 minutes north via CA-99 from our Tulare County shop.

Why does Fresno need a roofing company that specializes in foam? Because the local climate is a stress test that generic roofing systems fail early. Summer highs run past 100°F for weeks at a stretch, and a dark flat roof surface can hit 160°F or more — cooking asphalt, shrinking single-ply membranes, and driving cooling bills through the ceiling. Winter brings tule fog that keeps rooftops damp for days, so every seam, fastener, and flashing detail gets soaked and tested. Between the two seasons, relentless UV and airborne ag dust from the surrounding orchards and row crops grind away at whatever surface is up there. Spray foam roofing answers all of it at once: a seamless, self-flashing membrane with roughly R-6.5 of insulation per inch, finished with a UV-stable elastomeric or silicone topcoat that reflects the Valley sun instead of absorbing it.

We serve the whole Fresno metro, not just the city limits. Crews regularly work in Clovis, Sanger, Selma, Fowler, Kerman, and Kingsburg, and everything in between — the packing houses off CA-180 heading toward Sanger, the logistics and industrial parks of south Fresno, Calwa, and Malaga, metal ag buildings out toward Kerman on CA-180 west, and commercial strips along CA-41 and CA-168 through north Fresno and Clovis. If your building sits within sight of Highways 99, 41, 168, or 180, you are inside our normal service pattern. Being 45 minutes away — not four hours — also means the relationship survives the installation: warranty visits, recoat scheduling, and quick post-storm checks are a phone call, not a mobilization negotiation.

Four services cover nearly everything a Fresno building owner needs from us. Spray foam roofing is the flagship: new SPF systems installed over existing flat, low-slope, and metal roofs, typically $4–$8 per square foot installed. Silicone roof coating restores aging foam, metal, and smooth-surface roofs for a fraction of replacement cost — recoats usually run $2–$4 per square foot and reset the clock on a 10–20 year maintenance cycle. Roof repair handles leaks, ponding, blisters, and storm damage on foam and flat roofs; our long-standing Fresno foam roof repair page covers that service in depth, and it remains the fastest way to get a leaking Fresno roof looked at. Commercial spray foam insulation brings the same closed-cell chemistry inside — metal building walls and roof decks, warehouse ceilings, and cold storage envelopes where every degree of thermal control shows up on the utility bill.

Every engagement starts the same way, and it costs you nothing: a free assessment that includes a drone survey of the entire roof field, core sampling where the roof's history is unclear, and a written bid delivered within 48 hours. No pressure, no vague allowances — a documented scope you can hold us to. Because we are the installer and not a broker, the crew that quotes your Fresno roof is the crew network that shows up to do it, backed by industry-leading leak-proof guarantees.

Fresno rewards owners who think about roofs as energy equipment, not just weatherproofing. California's Title 24 energy code already pushes commercial re-roofs toward cool-roof surfaces, and PG&E summer demand charges punish buildings with under-insulated roof decks. An SPF roof addresses the code requirement and the operating cost in a single application — insulation, membrane, and reflective surface in one system. That is why so much of the Valley's food infrastructure, from cold storage docks to packing sheds, has quietly converted to foam over the past two decades.

We will put a drone over your roof, pull cores if the deck's condition is in question, and hand you a written number within two days — the same process whether you manage one storefront on Blackstone or a million square feet of distribution space in Malaga.

spray-foam-roofing.body_html:
Spray foam roofing in Fresno, CA solves the two problems every flat-roof owner in this city fights at once: brutal heat gain and a roof surface full of seams waiting to leak. Spray polyurethane foam (SPF) is applied as a liquid that expands into a seamless, fully-adhered blanket over your existing roof, curing in seconds into a rigid, closed-cell layer that insulates at roughly R-6.5 per inch and self-flashes around every curb, pipe, drain, and skylight. Topped with a UV-stable protective coating, it becomes a monolithic roof system with no laps, no fasteners, and no field seams — which in a climate like Fresno's is the difference between a roof that survives and a roof that needs a bucket brigade every time the weather turns.

Allstate Spray Foam has installed SPF across the Central Valley for more than twenty years. We are family-owned, Fully Licensed · Lic #C-2-1052735, BBB Accredited, and a Spray Polyurethane Foam Alliance member. Our crews reach Fresno in about 45 minutes, running north on CA-99 from our Tulare County shop, and we work the entire metro — Fresno proper, Clovis, Sanger, Selma, Fowler, Kerman, and Kingsburg.

What a Spray Foam Roof Actually Is

SPF starts as two liquid components mixed at the spray gun. On contact with the roof, the mixture expands about thirty times its volume and cures into rigid closed-cell foam within seconds. Because it is sprayed rather than rolled out in sheets, it conforms to whatever is up there — HVAC curbs, parapet transitions, pipe penetrations, sagging deck sections — and bonds directly to the substrate with no mechanical fasteners punching holes through your roof. The cured foam is then protected with an elastomeric or silicone topcoat, usually embedded with granules for durability, which shields the foam from UV and gives the roof its bright, reflective finish. The result is one continuous material from parapet to parapet. If you want the deeper technical background on the chemistry and system build-up, our spray polyurethane foam roofing guide covers it layer by layer.

Two properties make SPF unusual among roof systems. First, it is the only major roofing technology that is also insulation — the R-value is in the roof itself, not in a separate board layer that seams and joints can bypass. Second, it is renewable: when the topcoat wears after 10–20 years, you recoat rather than replace, and the foam underneath keeps performing indefinitely.

The Three Layers That Make Up the System

It helps to picture the finished roof as three cooperating layers. The substrate is whatever your building already has — built-up roofing, modified bitumen, concrete, plywood, or metal panels — cleaned, dried, and repaired so the foam has something sound to grip. The foam body is the structural heart: rigid closed-cell polyurethane, typically installed at one and a half inches or more, providing the insulation value, the slope corrections, and the seamless waterproofing plane. The coating and granule surface is the wear layer — the part Fresno's UV is allowed to attack, because it is designed to be sacrificial and renewable. Understanding that division of labor explains almost every maintenance recommendation we make: protect the coating and the foam never ages; let the coating go and you convert a cheap recoat into a repair project. It also explains why SPF quotes vary — each layer has a specification, and a low bid usually means one of the three has been quietly thinned.

Weight is worth a mention too, because Fresno has plenty of older buildings with tired structures: a complete SPF system adds well under a pound per square foot — a fraction of the load of a gravel-surfaced built-up roof or a concrete-paver ballasted system. On buildings where the structural engineer winces at adding another conventional roof layer, foam is frequently the only re-cover option that pencils without reinforcement work.

Fresno's Climate Is a Flat-Roof Stress Test

Fresno summers routinely stack up weeks of 100°F-plus days, and roof surface temperatures on dark membranes can exceed 160°F. That thermal load does three things: it drives heat straight into the building and onto your cooling bill, it accelerates the chemical aging of asphalt and single-ply membranes, and it makes every seam and fastener expand and contract daily until something opens up. Then winter arrives and the tule fog settles in — days of near-100% humidity that keep rooftops wet long enough to find every hairline opening the summer created. Add the constant film of ag dust blowing off the county's orchards, vineyards, and row crops, which holds moisture against the surface and clogs drains and scuppers, and you have a climate that destroys seamed roofing from both ends of the calendar.

SPF is unusually well matched to this. There are no seams to open. The foam's closed cells will not wick water. The reflective topcoat keeps surface temperatures dramatically lower than a dark membrane, cutting both heat gain and thermal cycling stress. And because foam is sprayed to slope, chronic low spots that pond after fog-drip and winter storms can be filled and pitched to drain during installation — a fix sheet goods simply cannot make.

Commercial Roofing in Fresno: Where SPF Fits

Most of our Fresno work is commercial roofing — the flat and low-slope decks that dominate the city's commercial building stock. Retail centers along the Blackstone Avenue corridor and Shaw Avenue, downtown office and mixed-use buildings, tilt-up warehouses in the south Fresno industrial belt, packing and processing plants toward Sanger and Selma, and metal-roofed shops from Kerman to Kingsburg all fall inside the same service pattern. SPF competes directly with TPO, PVC, modified bitumen, and built-up roofing on these buildings, and it usually wins on lifecycle cost because the insulation is included and the roof is renewable rather than disposable. For a broader look at how we approach commercial roofing in Fresno across all these system choices — including when we would honestly steer you away from foam — see our dedicated commercial roofing Fresno page. This page stays focused on the SPF system itself: what it is, what it costs, and how it behaves on Fresno buildings.

One commercial-specific advantage deserves emphasis: SPF installs over most existing roofs. That means no tear-off, no dumpsters cycling through your loading dock, no days where the deck is open to the sky, and in most cases no interruption to the business operating underneath. For a food processor or cold storage operator that cannot shut down, that is often the deciding factor.

Neighborhoods and Building Stock We Foam

Twenty years in the Valley means we have seen what is actually on Fresno's roofs, neighborhood by neighborhood:

  • South Fresno, Calwa, and Malaga industrial areas — big-box distribution, ag processing, and cold storage along the CA-99 spine. Huge flat decks, high internal heat or refrigeration loads, and owners who measure roofs in energy dollars. Prime SPF territory.
  • Blackstone Avenue and the Shaw corridor — mid-century retail strips with tired built-up roofs, multiple patch generations, and ponding. Foam levels the surface, buries the old seams, and gives these buildings a genuinely new roof without closing the stores below.
  • Downtown Fresno — older masonry office and warehouse buildings near Fulton Street with parapet walls, odd penetrations, and decades of roofing history. SPF's self-flashing behavior around parapets and details is at its best here.
  • Clovis and north Fresno along CA-168 — newer commercial and flex space where owners want cool-roof performance and Title 24 compliance on re-roofs.
  • Kerman, Kingsburg, Selma, Fowler, and Sanger — metal ag buildings, packing sheds, and shop buildings where foam solves rust-prone fastener leaks and condensation in one pass.

Knowing the building stock matters because SPF is specified to the building, not sold off a brochure. A 1960s built-up roof on Blackstone needs different prep and coring than a 1990s tilt-up in Malaga; a fog-belt packing shed near Sanger carries a different coating spec than a downtown office with parapet walls on four sides. Two decades of Valley roofs is the pattern library that makes our 48-hour bids accurate instead of padded — we have almost certainly already foamed a building like yours, within a few miles of yours.

Metal Building Roofing: The Retrofit Fresno's Ag Sector Runs On

A large share of the metro's ag infrastructure sits under corrugated or standing-seam metal — and aging metal roofs leak in a characteristic way: at thousands of fasteners and lap seams, all cycling with the Valley's daily temperature swing. Replacing metal panels is disruptive and expensive. Spraying foam directly over the metal is usually smarter: the foam locks down the panels, encapsulates every fastener head and lap, kills the rattle and thermal ping, adds R-6.5 per inch where the building had little or none, and stops the underside condensation that drips onto equipment during tule fog season. The foam also stiffens the roof diaphragm measurably. For packing houses around Sanger and Selma and shop buildings out toward Kerman, metal-over-foam retrofits are some of the most satisfying work we do — buildings that leaked at a hundred fasteners simply stop leaking.

What Spray Foam Roofing Costs in Fresno

Honest numbers, because budgeting a roof on vague ranges wastes everyone's time. A new SPF roof system installed over a prepared existing roof typically runs $4–$8 per square foot in the Fresno market. Where your project lands inside that range depends on foam thickness (driven by insulation goals and slope corrections), the condition and prep needs of the existing roof, detail density (a roof crowded with HVAC curbs costs more per foot than a clean deck), and coating specification. Recoating an existing foam roof — the scheduled maintenance event that renews the system — runs $2–$4 per square foot.

Free assessment & written bid$0Drone survey, core sampling where needed, bid in 48 hours

Compare those numbers against tear-off-and-replace pricing for membrane systems — which must also add insulation board to match SPF's thermal performance — and foam's lifecycle math usually speaks for itself. We break the whole calculation down, including energy payback, in our spray foam roofing cost guide.

Three cost factors deserve a closer look because they are where Fresno bids genuinely differ. Thickness is the biggest lever: foam sprayed at one and a half inches waterproofs; foam at two and a half or three inches waterproofs and meaningfully insulates, and the material difference shows in the price. Buildings with high cooling loads — most of them, in this city — usually come out ahead specifying more foam, because the energy delta pays for the increment. Existing roof condition is the second: a dry, sound deck needs cleaning and priming, while a roof with saturated sections needs those areas cut out and rebuilt before anything is sprayed, which is precisely what the core sampling in our free assessment is designed to find before the bid rather than as a change order after. Detail density is the third: every HVAC curb, pipe, drain, and skylight is hand-detail work, so a mechanical-heavy restaurant roof prices differently per foot than a clean warehouse field even at identical square footage. Our bids line-item all three, which is why they hold.

Energy Performance, R-Value, and Title 24

Every inch of SPF adds roughly R-6.5 of continuous insulation with zero thermal bridging — no fasteners conducting heat through the assembly, no board joints leaking air. On a Fresno warehouse or retail box running air conditioning against 100°F-plus outdoor air for four months a year, upgrading a nearly uninsulated roof deck to R-13 or R-20 of continuous foam changes the building's operating economics permanently. The reflective topcoat compounds the effect by rejecting solar gain before it enters the assembly at all; aged reflective coatings still bounce a large majority of solar energy compared with the 5–10% a black roof reflects.

California's Title 24 energy code is also in play on most Fresno commercial re-roof projects: low-slope re-roofs in our climate zone generally trigger cool-roof surface requirements, and SPF with a white silicone or elastomeric topcoat satisfies them as a matter of course. Rather than treating code compliance as an added cost line, an SPF roof folds it into the system you were buying anyway. We handle the paperwork realities of CA energy compliance on every bid — it is baked into how we specify coatings, not an afterthought.

How Installation Actually Goes

A typical Fresno SPF project runs in five stages. First, the assessment: drone survey of the full roof field, core sampling where the roof's build-up or moisture condition is uncertain, and a written bid within 48 hours. Second, preparation — the single biggest determinant of roof quality. We clean the surface (Fresno's ag dust film matters here; foam bonds to substrate, not to dust), address saturated areas found in coring, and prime where the substrate requires it. Third, foam application: the crew sprays in controlled passes, building thickness to spec and sloping foam into chronic ponding areas so water finally moves to the drains. Fourth, the protective topcoat goes on in multiple passes with embedded granules. Fifth, we walk the roof with you, document the installed system, and put the maintenance schedule in writing. Most Fresno projects, even large ones, proceed section by section so the building operates normally throughout. The full stage-by-stage detail lives on our spray foam roofing installation page.

Weather windows matter in the Valley: we plan around summer wind for overspray control and around winter fog for surface moisture, and we do not spray onto a damp deck. A crew that will spray through tule fog conditions is a crew whose foam will not stay bonded — scheduling discipline is part of the product.

Duration questions come up on every bid, so as honest orientation: production rate depends on prep scope and detail density far more than on raw square footage, and the drone survey lets us schedule realistically instead of optimistically. What we can promise on every Fresno project is sequencing that respects the business below — loading docks kept usable, exhaust and intake vents coordinated with your facilities staff, and overspray protection for the cars, equipment, and neighboring property around the building. Foam work done carelessly announces itself all over the parking lot; foam work done right is invisible until the utility bills arrive.

How Long a Foam Roof Lasts Here

The foam itself, kept coated, does not have a practical expiration date — SPF roofs from the 1970s are still in service nationally. What wears is the sacrificial topcoat, and in Fresno's UV that means a recoat roughly every 10–20 years depending on coating type and mils applied. Each recoat, at $2–$4 per square foot, resets the cycle without touching the foam. That renewability is the core of SPF's lifecycle advantage: you buy the roof once and maintain it forever, instead of buying a new roof every 15–20 years. We wrote up the full aging story, including what actually kills foam roofs (neglect, not weather), in how long does spray foam roofing last.

The Owner's Maintenance List Is Short

Between recoats, a Fresno foam roof asks very little of you, but the little it asks matters in this dust-and-fog climate:

  • Keep drains and scuppers clear — harvest-season dust and leaf litter are the usual culprits behind new ponding on an old roof.
  • Walk it twice a year and after major storms — you are looking for coating damage, punctures from dropped tools, or bird-pecked spots; caught early, each is a minutes-long caulk-grade fix.
  • Control rooftop traffic — HVAC techs with dropped screwdrivers cause more foam roof damage in Fresno than weather does; walk pads at service routes solve it.
  • Call us when the coating starts showing wear — a recoat scheduled on time costs $2–$4 per square foot; a recoat deferred until foam is exposed costs that plus repair work.

We put this schedule in writing at handover, and because our shop is 45 minutes away, having us walk the roof with you is a phone call, not a project.

SPF Against the Alternatives

Fresno owners usually price foam against TPO, and the comparison deserves straight talk. TPO is cheaper on day one for a plain, empty rectangle of roof. But TPO arrives in sheets, which means seams — miles of heat-welded seam on a big warehouse — and every seam is future maintenance in a climate with Fresno's thermal cycling. TPO also carries no insulation of its own, so matching SPF's thermal performance means adding polyiso board, which narrows the price gap fast. On detail-heavy roofs, roofs with ponding to correct, or buildings where energy cost matters, foam tends to win outright. We lay out the head-to-head honestly — including the cases where TPO is the right call — in spray foam vs TPO roofing.

Why Fresno Owners Call Allstate

Spray foam is an installer's product: the same chemistry applied by two different crews yields two very different roofs. Our case for your business is simple. Twenty-plus years of SPF work in this exact climate, family-owned accountability rather than a franchise chasing volume, full state licensing (Lic #C-2-1052735), BBB accreditation, SPFA membership, and industry-leading leak-proof guarantees on the systems we install. We are 45 minutes down CA-99, close enough that service after the sale is real — when a Fresno customer calls, a truck from our Tulare County shop is on your roof quickly, not "in the area next month."

The next step costs nothing: call (559) 739-9519 for the free assessment. Drone survey, core sampling where the roof's history warrants it, and a written bid in your hands within 48 hours. Whether you manage a Blackstone retail center, a Malaga distribution box, or a packing shed outside Kingsburg, you will know exactly what your roof needs and exactly what it costs — before you spend a dollar.
faqs: How much does spray foam roofing cost in Fresno?

New SPF roof systems in the Fresno market typically run $4-$8 per square foot installed over an existing roof, and recoats of existing foam run $2-$4 per square foot. The final number depends on foam thickness, roof prep, and detail density, which is why we put a written bid in your hands within 48 hours of the free drone assessment.
Can spray foam be installed over my existing Fresno flat roof without a tear-off?

In most cases, yes. SPF adheres directly over prepared built-up, modified bitumen, metal, and many single-ply roofs, so the business below keeps operating and nothing goes to the landfill. Core sampling during the free assessment tells us whether any saturated sections need to come out first.
How does a foam roof handle Fresno's 100-degree summers?

Better than any dark membrane. The reflective topcoat keeps surface temperatures far below a black roof, and the foam itself adds about R-6.5 of insulation per inch, so far less heat ever reaches the space below. Owners typically see the difference on their first summer PG&E bills.
Does tule fog or winter rain cause problems for SPF roofs?

Not for a properly installed one. Closed-cell foam does not absorb water and the system has no seams for fog-soaked winters to exploit. Weather matters during installation, though - we schedule around damp and windy conditions because foam must be sprayed onto a dry surface to bond correctly.
Do you also work outside Fresno city limits?
Yes. Clovis, Sanger, Selma, Fowler, Kerman, and Kingsburg are all part of our regular Fresno-area service pattern, and our crews dispatch about 45 minutes north via CA-99 from our Tulare County shop.
Is spray foam roofing compliant with California's Title 24 cool roof rules?

Yes. SPF finished with a white silicone or elastomeric topcoat meets the cool-roof surface requirements that apply to most low-slope commercial re-roofs in our climate zone, and we specify coatings with Title 24 compliance in mind on every Fresno bid.

silicone-roof-coating.body_html:
Silicone roof coating in Fresno, CA is the most cost-effective way to add 10–20 years of life to an aging flat, foam, or metal roof — without tear-off, without landfill fees, and usually without interrupting the business under it. A 100% silicone membrane is applied as a fluid over your existing roof and cures into a seamless, UV-immune, permanently flexible surface that sheds the Valley's brutal sun and shrugs off the ponding water that kills most other coatings. At $2–$4 per square foot for a typical recoat, it costs a fraction of replacement and resets your roof's maintenance clock.

Allstate Spray Foam has been coating Central Valley roofs for over twenty years. Family-owned, Fully Licensed · Lic #C-2-1052735, BBB Accredited, and an SPFA member, we run coating crews into Fresno, Clovis, Sanger, Selma, Fowler, Kerman, and Kingsburg — about 45 minutes north on CA-99 from our Tulare County shop.

What "100% Silicone" Means and Why It Matters

Not all roof coatings are close to equal. Acrylic coatings are water-based, cheaper, and genuinely useful in the right spot — but they re-emulsify under standing water and erode faster under UV. High-solids 100% silicone is a different animal: it is moisture-cure chemistry that is unaffected by ponding water, essentially immune to UV degradation, and stays flexible through Fresno's 100°F-plus summers and foggy near-freezing winters alike. On a flat roof in this climate — where drainage is rarely perfect and the sun is never merciful — silicone is the coating we specify most, because it is the one that is still performing in year fifteen. When we quote a silicone flat roof coating for a Fresno building, we quote high-solids 100% silicone at the manufacturer's specified millage, not a bargain blend stretched thin.

Millage and Granules: The Two Specs That Decide How Long It Lasts

Two specification lines separate a fifteen-year coating from a five-year one, and both are invisible once the roof is white. The first is dry-film thickness — coating performance and coating warranties are written in mils, and a system applied thin fails early no matter whose bucket it came from. We measure thickness during application rather than estimating by the bucket count, and the specified millage appears on your written bid where you can hold us to it. The second is granule embedment: broadcasting ceramic granules into the wet topcoat produces a tougher, higher-traction surface that resists foot traffic, hail bruising, and bird pecking, and it moderates silicone's two honest weaknesses — slickness when wet and dirt pickup. On Fresno roofs with regular HVAC service traffic, we recommend granules as a matter of course; the modest cost difference buys years of wear.

The Fresno Conditions a Roof Coating Has to Survive

Consider what a coated roof endures here in a single year. From June through September, surface temperatures cycle from warm mornings to a scorching afternoon peak day after day — the thermal expansion and contraction that cracks brittle coatings. UV exposure in the south Valley is among the most intense in the country, chalking and thinning lesser products year by year. Autumn drops ag dust from harvest across every horizontal surface in the county, clogging scuppers so winter water sits in ponds. Then tule fog season keeps the roof wet for days at a stretch, probing every pinhole while acrylics soften. A 100% silicone membrane is the only coating class that treats all of that as a normal Tuesday: ponded water cannot re-emulsify it, UV cannot meaningfully degrade it, and it stays elastic through every thermal cycle. That is why silicone dominates our Fresno recoat work from Blackstone Avenue retail to Malaga warehouses.

There is an energy dimension to all this heat as well. A fresh white silicone surface reflects the large majority of the solar energy that a weathered dark roof absorbs, which means the deck under it runs dramatically cooler on a 105°F afternoon and the rooftop HVAC equipment stops fighting a radiant oven all summer. California's Title 24 cool-roof requirements for low-slope re-roofs point in the same direction, and a silicone restoration typically satisfies them without any additional scope. For most Fresno owners the coating decision is made on leak protection and replacement avoidance — the summer utility relief and the code compliance arrive as bonuses in the same bucket.

Roof Coating Options for Fresno Buildings, Honestly Compared

Owners searching for roof coating in Fresno get pitched everything from asphalt emulsions to elastomerics, so here is the straight comparison we give on assessments:

CoatingPonding WaterUV ResistanceTypical Role in Fresno
100% SiliconeExcellent — unaffectedExcellentOur default for flat/foam/metal recoats
Acrylic elastomericPoor — re-emulsifiesGoodSloped metal with positive drainage, tight budgets
Aluminized asphaltPoorFairShort-term touch-up on old BUR only
UrethaneGoodFair — often topcoatedHigh-traffic zones, base coat under silicone

The pattern is simple: where a roof drains perfectly and the budget is tight, acrylic can earn its keep; everywhere water lingers — which on Fresno's aging flat roofs is nearly everywhere — silicone is worth the difference. We will tell you which one your roof actually needs, because a coating in the wrong application fails early and takes our reputation with it.

Hybrid specifications also exist and sometimes win: a urethane base coat for toughness under a silicone finish for UV and ponding immunity, or acrylic fields with silicone reserved for the pond-prone zones behind parapets. The point of an assessment done by an installer — rather than a coating salesman working a route — is that the specification follows the roof's actual conditions, drain by drain and low spot by low spot.

Silicone Roof Coating Pros and Cons

No product is perfect, and you should hear the cons from your contractor, not from the internet after you sign. The honest ledger:

  • Pro — ponding immunity: silicone is the only mainstream coating warrantied under standing water, which matters enormously on Fresno's older low-slope decks.
  • Pro — UV permanence: silicone does not chalk away in Valley sun the way acrylics do; its reflectivity fades slowly with dirt, not with degradation.
  • Pro — seamless and renewable: it flashes every detail monolithically, and when it finally wears, you clean and recoat directly over it — no future tear-off.
  • Pro — cost and speed: $2–$4 per square foot and days, not weeks, of installation with the building fully operating.
  • Con — slick when wet: cured silicone is slippery under fog-drip or rain; roofs with regular foot traffic get walk pads at hatches and service routes.
  • Con — dirt pickup: silicone holds dust, and Fresno has plenty; reflectivity benefits from an occasional rinse. Granule-embedded surfaces reduce this.
  • Con — adhesion is prep-critical: silicone bonds only to a properly cleaned, sound, dry substrate — and only new silicone sticks to old silicone. Prep discipline is most of the job.
  • Con — not a structural fix: coating does not repair a saturated roof. If core samples come back wet, those sections get addressed first or the coating is wasted money — we will say so.

Weigh that ledger against Fresno's specific conditions and the pros compound while the cons stay manageable. Slickness is solved with walk pads and granules; dirt pickup costs a little reflectivity, not waterproofing; prep discipline is a contractor-selection problem, not a product problem. Meanwhile the ponding immunity and UV permanence address exactly the two failure modes that end most Valley flat roofs. That asymmetry — cons you can engineer around versus pros that target your actual climate — is why silicone has become the default restoration spec across the region's commercial stock, and why the buildings that tried bargain acrylic on ponding decks a decade ago are calling us now.

What Silicone Roof Coating Costs in Fresno

Silicone roof coating price questions deserve real numbers. In the Fresno market, a silicone recoat on a sound roof runs $2–$4 per square foot. Position inside that range is driven by surface condition and cleaning needs (harvest-season dust and old coating chalk take real prep hours), how much cut-and-patch repair precedes the coating, specified dry-film thickness, and detail density — a roof crowded with HVAC curbs and penetrations takes more hand work per square than an open field. Compare that against $4–$8 per square foot for a new SPF system, or far more for tear-off and membrane replacement, and the economics of restoring rather than replacing are hard to argue with — provided the roof underneath is genuinely restorable, which is exactly what the free assessment establishes. Our spray foam roofing cost guide walks through the recoat-versus-replace math in detail.

Every Fresno coating bid we issue follows the same free process: drone survey of the whole field, core sampling where moisture is suspected, and a written scope and price within 48 hours. If a coating is the wrong answer for your roof, the assessment is where we tell you — before you have spent anything.

A note on how to compare bids, because coating quotes in the Fresno market can look identical on the surface and differ enormously underneath. Ask every bidder the same four questions: what dry-film thickness is being applied and how will it be verified; what repairs are included before coating begins; is the product high-solids 100% silicone or a blend; and what exactly does the guarantee cover, in writing. A per-square-foot number without those answers is not a bid — it is a guess you will finance. Our proposals answer all four on paper, which is precisely why we are comfortable being compared line for line against anyone working this market.

Recoating Foam Roofs: The Maintenance Cycle That Makes SPF Immortal

If your building already has a spray foam roof, silicone recoating is not an option — it is the scheduled event the whole system is designed around. The foam provides the insulation and the seamless waterproofing; the coating is the sacrificial UV shield that wears in its place. In Fresno sun, that shield lasts roughly 10–20 years depending on product and millage, and each $2–$4 per square foot recoat resets it completely without touching the foam beneath. Owners who keep that cycle never buy another roof; owners who skip it let UV reach the foam itself, and then the repair scope grows. The aging math is laid out in how long does spray foam roofing last, and the underlying system is explained in our spray polyurethane foam roofing guide. If your foam roof already has open blisters, exposed foam, or ponding damage, we handle that scope through our foam roof repair Fresno service before any coating goes down — coating over damage just hides it for a season.

Metal Roof Coating for the Metro's Ag and Industrial Buildings

Metal roof coating is its own discipline, and the Fresno area — with its packing sheds around Sanger and Selma, shop buildings out toward Kerman, and older industrial metal in Calwa and Malaga — has no shortage of candidates. Aging metal roofs fail at fasteners and lap seams: thousands of them, each backing out or rusting as panels cycle through the Valley's daily temperature swing. Our metal restoration process treats rust, seals every fastener head individually, bridges the lap seams with reinforcement, and then floods the whole field with silicone into one seamless membrane. The result stops existing leaks, prevents the next generation of them, and drops summer surface temperatures dramatically — metal buildings feel the reflective difference more than any other type because so many of them are barely insulated. Where a metal building also needs real R-value, we pair coating work with foam — see the metal retrofit section of our Fresno spray foam roofing service.

Owners of metal buildings often ask whether coating is worth doing on a roof that is already rust-streaked, and the answer depends on what the rust means. Surface oxidation on panels that are still structurally sound is exactly what restoration is for — it gets treated, primed, and sealed under the membrane, and the corrosion clock stops because water and oxygen no longer reach the steel. Panels rusted through, or purlin-level structural issues, are a different conversation, and the drone survey plus a hands-on walk tells us which building you have before anyone quotes anything. What we will not do is spray a bright white coat over failing steel to buy two quiet years — a coating should be the end of your leak story, not an intermission.

Buildings and Corridors Where We Coat

A sampling of where silicone work takes our crews in the metro: retail strips along Blackstone and Shaw with twenty-year-old built-up roofs that pond behind parapets; downtown Fresno offices where tear-off logistics over occupied space make restoration the only sane option; distribution and cold storage boxes in south Fresno and Malaga where owners want the reflectivity gain as much as the leak protection; Clovis flex-commercial along the CA-168 corridor hitting its first recoat window; and metal ag buildings from Kingsburg to Kerman with fastener leaks in the hundreds. The building types differ; the physics — UV, heat, dust, fog, imperfect drainage — are the same everywhere in Fresno County, and silicone answers all of them.

The substrates vary as much as the neighborhoods, and each gets its own prep protocol:

  • Aged spray foam — the natural recoat candidate; cleaned, spot-repaired, and recoated directly. This is the maintenance cycle SPF is designed around.
  • Built-up and modified bitumen — Fresno's most common older commercial roofs; asphalt bleed and chalk demand thorough washing and the right primer, but restored BUR is some of the best-value work we do.
  • Smooth single-ply (TPO/PVC/EPDM) — aging membranes with sound attachment can often be coated rather than torn off; adhesion testing during the assessment gives the yes or no.
  • Metal panels — fastener-by-fastener sealing plus seam reinforcement before the flood coat; the most transformation per dollar of any substrate we touch.
  • Previously coated roofs — old silicone takes new silicone after cleaning; old acrylic over-coats with silicone once chalk is washed off and adhesion is verified.

How a Coating Project Runs, Start to Finish

First the free assessment: drone survey, core samples where the deck's moisture history is unclear, written bid in 48 hours. Then preparation, which is most of the labor: pressure-washing the field (that ag-dust film again), drying, cutting out and patching failed areas, sealing seams and fasteners, and priming where the substrate demands it. Only then does silicone go down, sprayed or rolled in measured passes to the specified thickness, with detail work at every curb, drain, and penetration done by hand. We verify millage as we go — coating warranties are written in mils, and thin spots are where leaks are born. Most Fresno projects finish in days, the building operating underneath the whole time. Weather discipline matters here as much as on foam work: we do not coat wet steel or fog-damp decks, because adhesion is everything.

Timing a Coating Project Around the Fresno Calendar

The Valley gives coating crews a generous but not unlimited season. Late spring through early fall offers the long dry windows where production runs fastest — though peak-summer afternoons ask for early starts so material behaves on a hot deck. The window to respect is tule fog season: from roughly late November into February, decks can stay damp past midday, and moisture trapped under fresh coating is a blister factory. We schedule winter work around the fog rather than through it, and we tell owners plainly when a December call should become a January project. The practical advice: if your roof showed wear this summer, book the assessment now rather than after the first winter leak — the calendar is kindest to owners who plan one season ahead, and the free drone survey costs nothing to schedule.

What the Guarantee Actually Covers

Our silicone systems carry industry-leading leak-proof guarantees, and the written scope tells you exactly what stands behind them: the product installed, the millage applied, the repairs completed before coating, and the maintenance expected of the owner (chiefly keeping drains clear and calling us rather than a handyman when rooftop trades cut into the membrane). We would rather set those expectations in writing on day one than argue about them in year eight — and because we are family-owned and 45 minutes away, the name on the guarantee answers the phone.

Restore or Replace? The Question the Assessment Answers

The honest boundary: silicone restoration is for roofs that are aged but fundamentally sound — dry insulation, attached membrane, workable drainage. It is not for roofs whose insulation is waterlogged or whose substrate is failing; coating those is disguising a problem you will pay for twice. That is why our assessment includes core sampling and not just a walk-around. Roughly speaking, when a roof's wet area stays small, restoration wins economically by a wide margin; when saturation is widespread, we will show you the cores and talk about foam or replacement instead. Either way you get the evidence, the numbers, and a written recommendation — and the decision stays yours.

There is also a middle path worth knowing about: when a roof is too far gone for coating alone but the owner wants the seamless, renewable endgame, a new spray foam system over the existing deck delivers both — fresh insulation and waterproofing at $4–$8 per square foot, finished with the same silicone surface and entering the same 10–20 year recoat cycle. Plenty of our coating assessments end with that recommendation instead, and the same 48-hour written bid covers whichever scope the cores justify. The point of doing the diagnostics before the proposal is that you are choosing between real options priced from real evidence, not between a salesman's good-better-best sheet.

Our coating work carries industry-leading leak-proof guarantees, and our recommendation comes with core-sample evidence, not sales pressure. Call (559) 739-9519 and get the free drone assessment on the calendar — in 48 hours you will hold a written number for exactly what your Fresno roof needs.

commercial-insulation.body_html:
Commercial spray foam insulation in Fresno, CA turns the buildings that run this region's economy — metal shops, warehouses, packing houses, and cold storage — into envelopes that actually hold their conditioned air. Closed-cell spray polyurethane foam delivers roughly R-6.5 per inch, air-seals as it insulates, adds a vapor retarder in the same pass, and bonds structurally to metal panels and decking. In a county where summer highs sit above 100°F for weeks and PG&E demand charges punish every BTU of leakage, insulation is not a comfort upgrade; it is operating-cost equipment. Allstate Spray Foam has installed it across the Central Valley for more than twenty years — family-owned, Fully Licensed · Lic #C-2-1052735, BBB Accredited, SPFA member — and our rigs reach Fresno in about 45 minutes north on CA-99 from our Tulare County shop.

One boundary up front: our lane is commercial and agricultural work. Metal buildings, warehouses, processing plants, cold storage, shops, barns — not residential attics and crawlspaces. That focus is deliberate: commercial foam is rig-scale work with different chemistry choices, thickness specs, and code paths than house insulation, and it is what our crews do every week.

Closed-Cell Foam, Explained for Building Owners

Spray polyurethane foam arrives as two liquids that react at the gun and expand into place. Closed-cell foam — the commercial workhorse — cures rigid and dense, with its gas-filled cells sealed shut. Three consequences matter to a Fresno building owner. First, thermal performance: about R-6.5 per inch, roughly double fiberglass per inch of depth, so real R-values fit inside shallow metal-building cavities. Second, air sealing: foam expands into every gap, seam, and fastener penetration, and in most commercial buildings air leakage moves as much energy as conduction does. Third, moisture control: at typical thickness, closed-cell foam functions as its own vapor retarder and cannot wick or hold water. No other single material does all three jobs in one application — which is why the same chemistry, in a different formulation, is also what we install on roofs as spray polyurethane foam roofing.

Closed-Cell or Open-Cell? For Fresno Commercial Work, Usually Closed

Spray foam comes in two families, and the distinction matters enough to spell out. Open-cell foam is soft, light, and cheaper per inch, with an R-value around R-3.5–R-3.8 — a fine product for interior sound control and certain wall assemblies, but it absorbs water and offers no vapor control. Closed-cell foam is rigid and dense, carries roughly R-6.5 per inch, rejects moisture outright, and adds genuine structural stiffness to whatever it bonds to. For the buildings we insulate around Fresno — steel skins subject to condensation, warehouses under punishing cooling loads, cold storage where vapor drive is the whole battle — closed-cell is the correct specification nearly every time, and it is what our commercial rigs run. When a scope genuinely suits open-cell (an interior partition wall, a sound-control ceiling), we say so and price it honestly; what you will not get from us is open-cell quoted where closed-cell physics is required, just to win on price.

Fire Code and Thermal Barriers, Stated Plainly

Building code treats spray foam as a combustible plastic, which means foam in occupied spaces generally must be separated from the interior by a thermal barrier — half-inch drywall or an approved equivalent — or covered with an intumescent coating rated for the purpose, with specific allowances and exceptions depending on the building and occupancy. This is not fine print to discover at inspection time; it is a design input that belongs in the bid. Our proposals for Fresno projects state how ignition and thermal barrier requirements will be met for your specific occupancy — coating, board, or existing assembly — so the price you compare includes the code path, not just the foam. Any bidder who waves the topic off is quoting you a change order in advance.

Metal Buildings: Fresno's Most Under-Insulated Square Footage

Drive any corridor out of the city — CA-180 west toward Kerman, CA-99 south through Fowler and Selma, Golden State Boulevard past the older industrial stock — and you pass thousands of steel buildings insulated with either sagging vinyl-faced blanket or nothing at all. Bare metal skins mean interiors that track the outdoors: 110°F-plus inside on July afternoons, dripping condensation during tule fog season as warm moist interior air hits cold panels. Closed-cell foam sprayed directly to the walls and roof deck fixes the whole failure pattern at once. It insulates at R-6.5 per inch, glues the panel system together (adding measurable rigidity), encapsulates every through-fastener, and — because the foam surface stays near room temperature — ends the condensation drip that rusts equipment and stains inventory. For shops, equipment barns, and packing sheds around Sanger, Selma, Kingsburg, and Kerman, a foam retrofit is routinely the difference between an unusable summer building and a workable one.

Retrofit details matter on these buildings, and twenty years of them has taught us the traps. Existing vinyl-faced blanket usually comes down before foam goes up — spraying over compressed, dust-laden batt buries a future problem. Panel seams and skylight curbs get inspected for active leaks first, because insulation should never be the thing hiding a roof problem; where the roof itself is the patient, a foam roof from above may be the smarter scope. Lighting and electrical runs get coordinated so conduit stays serviceable. None of this is exotic — it is the difference between an insulation contractor in Fresno who does metal buildings weekly and a crew improvising its first one on yours.

Warehouses and Distribution Space Along the 99 Spine

South Fresno, Calwa, and Malaga carry the metro's logistics load — tilt-up and steel distribution boxes feeding the CA-99 corridor. Most were built with minimal roof-deck insulation, and their owners pay for it every summer as rooftop units fight heat radiating off the deck all afternoon. Spraying closed-cell foam to the underside of the roof deck (or foaming the roof from above — often the smarter move; see below) transforms the load calculation. The same applies to dock walls, where seams and panel joints leak conditioned air around the clock. For tenants under triple-net leases and owners marketing space, insulation performance shows up directly in the operating-expense line that Fresno's industrial market increasingly quotes. Warehouse projects are also where staging matters most: our crews work in sections, coordinate around racking and inventory, and keep the facility receiving while we spray.

The metro's other commercial stock benefits just as directly, even if it calls us less often. Downtown Fresno's older masonry buildings being repositioned as offices, studios, and event space frequently have uninsulated roof structures that make conditioning economics impossible until foam changes them. Back-of-house areas in Blackstone and Shaw corridor retail — stockrooms, prep kitchens, mechanical mezzanines — are routinely the envelope holes through which a storefront's cooling budget escapes. Churches, gyms, and shop-with-office buildings across Clovis, Fowler, and Selma share the same profile: big simple volumes, thin envelopes, and owners staring at summer bills that insulation would cut permanently. If the building has a cooling load and a metal or under-insulated shell, the physics — and the fix — are the same.

Cold Storage and Ag Processing: Where Every Degree Is Money

Fresno County's packing and processing plants — fruit off the east-side orchards through Sanger and Selma, and the cold chain that moves it — run refrigeration as their dominant utility cost. In cold storage, insulation defects do not merely waste energy; they build ice, and ice on evaporators, ceilings, and door frames is a defrost, maintenance, and safety problem. Closed-cell foam is the standard answer because it insulates and vapor-seals simultaneously: warm, humid outside air (or fog-season air) never reaches a cold surface inside the assembly to condense and freeze. We foam cooler and freezer envelopes, dock transitions, processing-room ceilings, and the chronically troublesome penetrations where refrigeration lines pass through walls. On these projects thickness specs come from dew-point math, not rules of thumb — under-speccing a freezer wall by an inch shows up as frost within a season, so we engineer it right the first time.

Timing is the other cold-chain reality: packing houses live and die by the harvest calendar, and an insulation crew that wants your cooler offline in August does not understand the business. We plan these projects for the off-season windows the operation actually has, sequence work zone by zone so product keeps moving, and coordinate with your refrigeration contractor so defrost cycles and door schedules are not fighting the installation. It is unglamorous logistics, but it is why food-side operators keep our number.

Spray Foam Against Fiberglass: The Comparison That Decides Most Projects

Nearly every Fresno insulation bid we win was previously specced as fiberglass batt or blanket, so here is the honest head-to-head:

FactorClosed-Cell Spray FoamFiberglass Batt / Blanket
R-value per inch~R-6.5~R-2.9–R-3.8
Air sealingBuilt in — expands into gapsNone — air moves through and around it
Vapor controlOwn vapor retarder at thicknessNeeds separate facing; fails at seams
Moisture behaviorClosed cells — will not absorb or sagAbsorbs, sags, loses R-value when damp
Fit to metal buildingsBonds to panels, seals fasteners, adds rigidityCompressed at every purlin, gaps at details
Upfront costHigherLower
Lifecycle in Valley conditionsDecades, stableDegrades with dust, moisture, pests, sag

Fiberglass wins exactly one line of that table. In a climate with 100°F-plus cooling seasons, fog-season condensation risk, and ag dust that infiltrates every unsealed assembly, the performance lines are the ones that compound year after year. Where a budget genuinely cannot reach foam everywhere, hybrid designs — foam at the roof deck and rim details, batt in easy wall bays — capture most of the benefit; we spec those honestly too.

The Benefits Nobody Puts on the Utility Bill

Beyond R-value and air sealing, closed-cell foam earns its keep in Fresno buildings in quieter ways:

  • Dust exclusion — the Valley's ag dust rides infiltrating air into every unsealed building; foam closes the paths, which packing houses and food-adjacent operations notice immediately in housekeeping and compliance terms.
  • Pest and bird exclusion — the gaps at panel laps, eaves, and penetrations that let air through let starlings and rodents through too; a foamed envelope removes the openings entirely.
  • Structural stiffening — closed-cell foam bonded to metal panels measurably stiffens the assembly, calming panel drum and rattle in wind.
  • Quieter interiors — insulation across a metal skin knocks down both outside noise and the interior echo of a bare steel box, a real quality-of-work-life change on a production floor.
  • Condensation-driven corrosion stops — with interior air kept off cold steel, the slow rust bloom at fasteners and laps stops progressing, protecting the building itself.

What Commercial Spray Foam Costs in the Fresno Market

Commercial insulation is bid to the project, not off a rate card, because the honest drivers vary: total square footage and mobilization scale, specified thickness (an R-13 shop wall and an R-40 freezer ceiling are different animals), substrate prep, masking and overspray protection around equipment and inventory, and access height. As orientation, closed-cell foam is typically priced per board foot — one square foot at one inch thick — and multi-inch commercial assemblies land at a few dollars per square foot in most Valley projects, scaling with thickness. What we commit to is the process: a free assessment of your building, and a written, line-itemed bid within 48 hours, so the number you plan around is real. Cost-per-square-foot logic, and how thickness drives it, is explained further in our spray foam roofing cost guide — the same math governs insulation work.

Payback context matters more than the sticker: on a metal building going from bare skin to R-13+ walls and roof, summer cooling loads drop so sharply that many Fresno owners see the project pay for itself within a handful of PG&E summers — and Title 24 compliance on alterations comes along with it rather than as a separate fight.

Two budgeting habits make these projects go well. First, spec to the load, not to the minimum: the marginal cost of another inch of foam is mostly material, while the mobilization, masking, and labor are already paid for — so the cheapest R-value you will ever buy is the inch you add during the original project. Second, get the whole envelope assessed even if you only intend to insulate part of it; knowing that the roof deck is the dominant loss path (it usually is, in this climate) prevents spending the budget on walls that were never the problem. The free assessment covers both questions before any money moves.

Title 24 and the Code Reality for Fresno Projects

California's Title 24 energy standards apply to most commercial construction and many alterations in Fresno County, setting minimum envelope performance for conditioned buildings. Closed-cell foam makes compliance straightforward rather than marginal: continuous insulation values are met in fewer inches, and the air-sealing performance foam delivers is exactly the direction the code keeps moving. For unconditioned ag-exempt buildings, code may not force insulation — but refrigeration economics and worker conditions usually argue louder than the code does. We handle the documentation on every bid where Title 24 applies, and we will tell you plainly when it does not.

Choosing an Insulation Contractor in Fresno: What Actually Matters

Spray foam is unforgiving of bad installation — off-ratio chemistry, wrong substrate temperatures, or rushed passes produce foam that shrinks, smells, or delaminates, and no warranty paperwork fixes it afterward. So when you evaluate any insulation contractor in Fresno, including us, check four things. State licensing you can verify (ours: Lic #C-2-1052735). Track record in commercial foam specifically — ask how many metal buildings and cold storage envelopes the crew has done, not just houses. Industry affiliation (we are SPFA members; the Alliance publishes the standards good installers work to). And a written scope that names product, thickness, and prep — not a per-foot number scribbled on a card. Twenty-plus years, family ownership, and BBB accreditation are our answers to those questions; we encourage you to ask them of anyone who bids against us.

Proximity is the fifth factor Fresno owners underrate until they need it. Spray foam is equipment-intensive work — rigs, proportioners, generators, hose heat — and a contractor trucking in from the Bay Area or Southern California prices every mobilization and disappears after the last one. Our shop sits 45 minutes down CA-99, which changes the economics of everything after the sale: warranty visits, small additions when you expand the building, a quick look when your facilities manager notices something odd. Buying foam from the company that will still be nearby in year fifteen is cheaper than it looks on bid day.

How an Installation Runs in an Operating Facility

Most of our Fresno insulation work happens in buildings that cannot shut down, so the process is built around it. Assessment first — we walk the facility, identify substrate and prep needs, and deliver the written bid within 48 hours. Scheduling gets planned around your operation: sections, shifts, or weekends as the facility requires. Prep is masking and protection — inventory, equipment, and finished surfaces get covered, and ventilation is set up per SPFA practice. Application runs in controlled lifts to the specified thickness, with depth checked as we go. Re-occupancy of sprayed zones follows the product's cure schedule — we state those windows up front so operations can plan, and the rest of the facility runs normally throughout. The mechanics are similar to our roof work, which is detailed on the spray foam roofing installation page; interior work adds the masking and ventilation discipline.

Quality is verified as we go, not assumed at the end: depth gauges confirm thickness against the spec in every zone, and pass thicknesses stay within the product's lift limits — foam installed in over-thick single passes can scorch or shrink, which is an installer-discipline failure no warranty paperwork repairs. At completion you receive documentation of what went on your walls and deck: product, thickness, and coverage — the paper trail that matters for Title 24 files, insurance questions, and the day you sell or refinance the building.

Insulate the Roof From Above Instead: One System, Two Jobs

Here is advice that regularly saves Fresno owners money: if your roof is also near the end of its life, do not buy interior deck insulation and a re-roof separately. A spray foam roof installed from above is both — a seamless waterproof membrane and R-6.5 per inch of continuous insulation over the deck, with no interior disruption, no masking around racking, and no lost operating hours. For warehouses and processing plants whose roofs and energy bills are failing together, that single system is usually the best capital allocation on the table. Spray foam insulation in Fresno, in other words, sometimes belongs on top of the building rather than inside it — the assessment tells us which, and the two service pages together show the full picture.

The decision logic is straightforward. If the roof membrane has ten good years left and the pain is purely thermal, interior deck foam wins — it is cheaper per R and leaves the roof alone. If the roof is leaking or within a recoat-or-replace decision anyway, foam from above wins decisively, because you were about to spend roofing money regardless and the insulation arrives inside the same $4–$8 per square foot system. And if the building needs both wall insulation and a roof, bundling them into one mobilization saves real money over two separate projects a year apart. We quote the scopes separately and together so the comparison is yours to make with actual numbers.

Get the Building Assessed — It Costs Nothing

Whether it is a Kerman equipment barn, a Malaga distribution box, a Selma packing line, or a downtown Fresno building being repositioned, the first step is identical: call (559) 739-9519. We assess the building free, spec the assembly honestly — foam where foam earns it, hybrid where that is smarter — and put a written bid in your hands within 48 hours. Family-owned, twenty-plus years in the Valley, Fully Licensed · Lic #C-2-1052735, BBB Accredited, SPFA member, and 45 minutes up CA-99 whenever your building needs us.
